checks.note: The proposition says the participants were 'people using AI tools without coding knowledge'. The quoted sentence does not say this, and the contract says that description is not established. The cited article shows Attempt one was by a software developer. The citation excerpts are cut to single words: 'bugs' drops 'Sorting out the bugs was frustrating' and 'easy' drops 'surprisingly'. With explanations of only 'Supports.' and 'Qualifies.', readers can't tell what was found. All the evidence comes from one attempt (Attempt two).

The excerpt, proposition, 'soon' horizon and 'most or all' threshold all match. Stack Overflow's 51% daily use and JetBrains' 85% figure (100% minus the 15% who had not adopted, from April–June 2025 fieldwork) support majority adoption within months. The e2 excerpt '15% of developers' is short, but its explanation states the 85% complement. Outcome supported and horizon conclusive_event match the agreed reviews.
